key_insight: Magic state injections enable universal transversal quantum computing while keeping sequential decoding volumes statistically bounded in the random circuits studied.
engineering_relevance: Sequential decoding could make space-time correlated error correction more scalable by preventing decoding instances from growing with total circuit volume.
method: Backpropagate logical measurement operators to construct space-time decoding graphs.
Decode measurements sequentially, commit corrections, and exclude previously processed syndrome data.
Compare decoding volumes across measurement-product choices, circuit connectivities, and Clifford gate ensembles.
evidence_signal: For random circuits, mid-circuit decoding volumes approach a stationary average set by magic state injection density, with exponentially suppressed large instances and similar qualitative behavior across tested circuit variants.
watch_item: Stationary decoding volumes in random circuits do not alone establish practical decoder latency or performance for structured quantum algorithms.
paper_title: Bounded decoding complexity in transversal circuits with magic state injection
